title: We Come with Joy and Gladness
description: We Come with Joy and Gladness in Tonic Solfa to GREENLAND, doh is Eb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: These words were printed without an author's name in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 755 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Anniversary of Independence”, where the book credits them to the Boston S. S. H. Book.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Sevens and Sixes Double (7.6.7.6.7.6.7.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to GREENLAND; any other Sevens and Sixes Double tune fits them as well.
underlay: We come with joy and glad-ness To breathe our songs of praise, Nor let one note of sad-ness Be min-gled in our lays; For 'tis a hal-lowed sto-ry, This theme of free-dom's birth: Our fa-thers' deeds of glo-ry Are e-choed round the earth.

lines: We come with joy and gladness
To breathe our songs of praise,
Nor let one note of sadness
Proud men shall rule no longer,
For God the Lord is near:
And then shall sink the mountains
Where pride and power are crowned,
O God! we would adore thee,

licence: Public domain: anonymous words in print by 1853.
credits: Words anonymous, public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to GREENLAND by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
